newsitem.title: USA: Stocks end up amid flood of IPOs.
newsitem.headline: Stocks end up amid flood of IPOs.

text.p: Stocks eked out small gains Friday as the market digested more than a dozen initial public offerings and investors braced for a spate of economic reports next week.

"We had a tidal wave of IPOs. But this market seems to be in a long pause. There's a lack of conviction and we have a good deal more economic reports next week," said Marty Kearney, a trader at PTI Securities.
The Dow Jones industrial average rose 4.07 to 5,872.92. For the week, the Dow fell 15.54 points.
In the broader market, advancing issues led declines 1,291 to 1,010 on heavy volume of 407 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.
Kearney said the Dow has climbed more than 4 percent so far in September, not bad for what is historically the weakest month of the year.
The Nasdaq Composite index rose 2.07 to 1,230.05, drawing nearer to June 5's record high of 1,249.15. The index was up 10.36 on the week.

The long bond lost a quarter point to yield 6.91 percent, up from 6.88 percent on Thursday. Treasuries fell on profit-taking after a strong run this week following the Federal Reserve's decision on Tuesday to hold interest rates steady.

Wall Street next week faces a slew of economic reports, including the National Association of Purchasing Management index for September, August new home sales and leading indicators and Friday's key September employment data.

"Stocks are straggling on fears of a slowdown in the fourth quarter. But as in the past there's the usual difficulty for the market in reaching the next plateau, in this case 6,000" for the Dow, said Peggy Farley, chief executive officer of Amas Securities.

"We had a full calendar of IPOs this week with the last part of the week not showing as good a performance as they should have," she said. "The euphoria the (IPO) market saw in the spring has dissipated, there's less confidence."

Stocks debuting Friday included Spanish-language TV broadcaster Univision Communications, up 8-1/2 to 31-1/2, and Swiss watch maker Tag Heuer International, which rose to 20 on the NYSE from its $19.55 a share pricing.

IPOs Cox Radio Inc surged 3-1/2 to 22 and sunglasses maker Gargoyles rallied 4-9/16 to 20-9/16. RockShox, a maker of bicycle suspension products, rose 1/4 to 15-1/4, and Lightbridge rose 1-5/8 to 11-5/8.
Among other newly public companies, temporary staffing company StaffMark rose two to 14, Nitinol Medical was up 1/4 to 11-1/4 and CellNet Data fell to 19 from its $20 pricing.

As for the overall market, "the action has been quite good. It was a very volatile week and a lot of that volatility has been constructive in helping to arrest excesses," said Eugene Peroni, chief technical analyst with Janney, Montgomery Scott.
Among other issues, Dow component GE rose 1-1/8 to 91-1/2. Goldman Sachs upgraded GE to the firm's recommended list.
PepsiCo slumped 2-1/8 to 28-1/8 after warnings that 1997 earnings will lag analysts' forecasts by 10 cents a share.
The Standard & Poor's index of 500 stocks rose 0.33 of a point to 686.19, down 0.82 on the week.
The NYSE composite inched up 0.28 to 366.27, topping Thursday's record 365.99. The index rose 0.5 from last Friday.
The average price per share rose 3 cents.
The American Stock Exchange index rose 1.28 to 568.47, up 3.27 on the week.
The Wilshire Associates Equity Index -- the market value of NYSE, American and Nasdaq issues -- was 6,754.329, up 5.197 or 0.08 percent. It was up 18.13 on the week.
